method: independent per-page assessment with pypdf (a different extractor from pdf-inspector): every page's extractable text was measured and image-only pages detected; all 17 documents, all pages — no sampling was needed at this collection size. The private per-page detail is output/.page_assessment.private.json (gitignored).
label_rule: needs_ocr=true when the pipeline's extraction misses usable content at or above the approved 10% page tolerance; the pypdf cross-check distinguishes 'no text layer' from 'extractor failure'

dev_001.pages_without_usable_text: 3 of 991 (0.3%) — image pages; text layer healthy elsewhere (median 1,158 chars/page)
dev_001.note: the exp-28 false route; under the approved 10% tolerance it does not warrant OCR

dev_002.pages_without_usable_text: 23 of 23 (100%) — scanned image pages, no text layer

dev_003.pages_without_usable_text: 0 of 17 under pypdf — but pdf-inspector extracted zero characters on all 17 in experiment 28
dev_003.note: Sloman 1971: NOT a scan — a pdf-inspector extraction failure on a real text layer (pypdf median 2,944 chars/page). Labelled needs_ocr=true because the pipeline's own extractor misses all content; the fallback exists precisely for this failure mode.

coverage_disclosure: all pages of all 17 documents assessed via the independent extractor; the held-out split contains no needs_ocr=true document, so held-out recall is untestable by construction — disclosed, not hidden
